name: CA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Minimal Republican spending or outside support
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean, DeSaulnier's incumbency, and his clear fundraising advantage over Jeff Frese point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and prediction markets price the race at 96% Democratic. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much closer race or unexpected outside spending on Frese would warrant a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark DeSaulnier seeks another term in a Bay Area district that leans Democratic by 18 points. He advanced to the general with a large fundraising edge, holding about $586,000, while Republican Jeff Frese has reported little financial activity and no outside groups are spending in the race. Prediction markets give DeSaulnier roughly a 96% chance of winning.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and money. Those fundamentals point to a safe Democratic seat, with the main uncertainty being the wide error band that comes from a race with so little direct data.
